_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with metastatic small cell lung cancer (SCLC) with disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, single-arm, non-randomized, multi-cohort basket trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with metastatic SCLC who had disease progression on or after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Investigator-assessed confirmed overall response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1
pivotal_trials.result: Investigator-assessed ORR 35% (95% CI: 26, 45) with median DOR 5.3 months (95% CI: 4.1, 6.4); IRC-assessed ORR 30% (95% CI: 22, 40) with median DOR 5.1 months (95% CI: 4.9, 6.4)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%, including lab abnormalities) were leukopenia, lymphopenia, fatigue, anemia, neutropenia, increased creatinine, increased ALT, increased glucose, thrombocytopenia and nausea. Grade 3/4 neutropenia occurred in 41% and febrile neutropenia in 7%; serious adverse reactions occurred in 34% of patients. Key warnings are myelosuppression and hepatotoxicity.
target_moa: Lurbinectedin is an alkylating drug that inhibits oncogenic transcription by binding covalently to GC-rich DNA sequences, causing double-strand DNA breaks leading to cell death

rems.type: There were no significant safety concerns identified during the review requiring risk management beyond labeling or warranting consideration for a REMS

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application did not raise significant safety, efficacy, or public health questions and the drug is not first in its class

description.text: Added Zepzelca in combination with atezolizumab (or atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs) for maintenance treatment of adult extensive-stage SCLC not progressed after first-line induction therapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for the use of Zepzelca (lurbinectedin) intravenous infusion, in combination with atezolizumab or atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs, for the maintenance treatment of adult patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer in whose disease has not progressed after first-line induction therapy with atezolizumab or atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs, carboplatin, and etoposide.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR)

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response [see *Clinical Studies (14)*]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s).

confirmatory_requirement.text: PMR 3831-1: Submit the final report and datasets for the OS and PFS analysis (IRC-determined) from a clinical trial to confirm clinical benefit of lurbinectedin in SCLC; the review notes this could be from the ATLANTIS trial

citations.quote: 3831-1 Submit the final report and datasets for the overall survival and progression-free survival analysis as determined by an Independent Review Committee from a clinical trial to confirm the clinical benefit of lurbinectedin in small cell lung cancer that may inform product labeling.

This could be from the Study titled, "Phase III Randomized Clinical Trial of Lurbinectedin (PM01183)/Doxorubicin Versus Cyclophosphamide, Doxorubicin and Vincristine (CAV) or Topotecan as Treatment in Patients With Small-Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC) Who Failed One Prior Platinum-containing Line (ATLANTIS)".

orphan_indication.text: Orphan-drug designation granted for lurbinectedin for the treatment of SCLC on August 1, 2018

summary.text: ZEPZELCA (lurbinectedin) received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 (Subpart H) for metastatic SCLC based on ORR and DOR from a single-arm cohort of Study B-005, with a required confirmatory trial (ATLANTIS) to verify clinical benefit. The application had orphan-drug designation and was reviewed under Priority review; it was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: The recommendation for accelerated approval, according to 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H, is based on the results from a single trial, PM1183-B-005-14 (Study B-005), an ongoing, multicenter, open-label, non-randomized, multi-cohort trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of lurbinectedin as a single-agent in adult patients with advanced solid tumors.

This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s).
Pharma Mar was granted orphan-drug designation for lurbinectedin for the treatment of SCLC on August 1, 2018.

requirement.text: 3831-1: Submit the final report and datasets for the overall survival and progression-free survival analysis (IRC-determined) from a clinical trial to confirm the clinical benefit of lurbinectedin in SCLC (accelerated approval confirmatory requirement)

citations.quote: 3831-1 Submit the final report and datasets for the overall survival and progression-free survival analysis as determined by an Independent Review Committee from a clinical trial to confirm the clinical benefit of lurbinectedin in small cell lung cancer that may inform product labeling.

requirement.text: 3831-2: Submit the final report of PBPK modeling with results from a drug interaction trial with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor to assess the effect of a moderate CYP3A inhibitor on lurbinectedin exposure and appropriate dosage recommendations

citations.quote: 3831-2 Submit the final report of a physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling with the results from the drug interaction trial with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, to assess the effect of concomitant administration of a moderate CYP3A inhibitor on lurbinededin exposure, that will determine the magnitude of increase in the exposure of lurbinededin and appropriate dosage recommendation for patients receiving concomitant medications that are moderate CYP3A inhibitors, that may inform labeling.

requirement.text: 3831-3: Submit analysis and datasets with the final report from a hepatic impairment clinical trial to evaluate PK and safety of lurbinectedin in patients with mild, moderate, or severe hepatic impairment and determine appropriate dosage recommendations

citations.quote: 3831-3 Submit the analysis and datasets with the final report from a hepatic impairment clinical trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetics and safety of lurbinededin in patients with mild, moderate, or severe hepatic impairment and determine the magnitude of increase exposure and appropriate dosage recommendations, that may inform product labeling.

requirement.text: 3831-4: Submit the final report and datasets from a clinical PK trial to assess the effect of itraconazole (strong CYP3A inhibitor) on lurbinectedin in patients with advanced solid tumors and determine appropriate dosage recommendations

citations.quote: 3831-4 Submit the final report and datasets from a clinical pharmacokinetic trial to assess the potential effects of Itraconazole on lurbinededin in patients with advanced solid tumors and determine the magnitude of increase exposure and appropriate dosage recommendation of lurbinededin when administered concomitantly with strong CYP3A inhibitors, that may inform product labeling.

requirement.text: 3831-5: Submit the final analysis of ORR and DOR with datasets for the SCLC cohort enrolled in study PM1183-B-005-14 to provide additional long-term efficacy data

citations.quote: 3831-5 Submit the final analysis of overall response rate and duration of response along with the datasets for the small cell lung cancer cohort enrolled in study PM1183-B-005-14 titled; "Clinical Trial of Lurbinectedin in Selected Advanced Solid Tumors" to provide additional long-term efficacy data that may inform product labeling.

requirement.text: 3831-6: Submit the final report from a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of repeat doses of a moderate CYP3A inducer on single-dose PK of lurbinectedin and determine appropriate dosage recommendations for concomitant moderate CYP3A inducers

citations.quote: 3831-6 Submit the final report from a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of repeat doses of a moderate CYP3A inducer on the single dose pharmacokinetics of lurbinectedin and to determine the magnitude of decrease in lurbinectedin exposure, and appropriate dosage recommendation when lurbinectedin is coadministered with moderate CYP3A inducers, that may inform product labeling.
